guide.title: Barkhamsted, Connecticut: A Reservoir, a Chair Factory and a Lighthouse
guide.intro: Barkhamsted was among the last Connecticut towns European colonists settled: the colony's 1756 census counted just 18 residents, still only 250 by 1774. Windsor proprietors received the land in a 1732 colonial reorganization and divided it into five lots among 108 shareholders; the town applied for incorporation in 1774 but wasn't recognized until 1779, taking its name from Berkhamsted, England, home to many early settlers. Around 1740, Mary "Molly" Barber and James Chaugham, a Narragansett man, founded a mixed-race settlement on the Farmington River that stagecoach drivers nicknamed "the Lighthouse" for the light from their home. In 1819, Lambert Hitchcock opened a chair factory pioneering interchangeable parts in the village that became Hitchcocksville, renamed Riverton in 1866. The Metropolitan District Commission later flooded Barkhamsted Hollow for the 30-billion-gallon Barkhamsted Reservoir, completed in 1944 and costing roughly 1,000 residents their homes.

sections.heading: A lighthouse village and a chair factory
sections.body: Long before Hitchcocksville existed, the Lighthouse community survived on the Farmington River in poverty until the mid-1800s, its cellar holes and gravestones now protected within Peoples State Forest as a State Archaeological Preserve. Lambert Hitchcock's 1819 chair factory pioneered mass-produced interchangeable parts, and the mill village he built renamed itself Riverton in 1866; the Old Riverton Inn, originally Ives Tavern and dating from 1796, still anchors the village. Squire's Tavern, the Barkhamsted Historical Society's headquarters, also stewards Merrill Tavern and the Center Schoolhouse.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Barkhamsted is car country in the Litchfield Hills: U.S. Route 44 crosses the town's southwestern corner, with state Routes 20, 181, 219 and 318 branching off to reach Pleasant Valley, Riverton, Lake McDonough and the state forests. There is no rail station and no public transportation in town — the automobile is the principal way to get around, and the nearest CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak stop is Hartford Union Station.

sections.heading: Two forests on the Farmington River
sections.body: Peoples State Forest and American Legion State Forest sit across the West Branch Farmington River from each other, together offering hiking, fishing, canoeing and the region's best cross-country skiing and snowmobiling; Peoples' stone Nature Museum, built by the CCC in 1935, keeps seasonal hours. Below Saville Dam, the Metropolitan District Commission runs Lake McDonough for boating and fishing, though its swimming beach remains closed for a lifeguard shortage. In Riverton, the Royal Coachman Tavern serves the Old Riverton Inn's dining room, and the Riverton General Store makes sandwiches near both.

faq.question: How do I get to Barkhamsted?
faq.answer: By car — U.S. Route 44 crosses the southwestern corner of town, with state Routes 20, 181, 219 and 318 branching off it. There's no passenger rail station or public transportation in Barkhamsted; the nearest CTrail Hartford Line and Amtrak stop is Hartford Union Station.

faq.question: What was "the Lighthouse"?
faq.answer: A mixed-race community founded around 1740 by Mary "Molly" Barber, a white woman from Wethersfield, and James Chaugham, a Narragansett man from Block Island. Stagecoach drivers nicknamed it for the light from their home; the site survived, largely in poverty, until the mid-1800s and is now a protected State Archaeological Preserve within Peoples State Forest.

faq.question: Can I swim at Lake McDonough?
faq.answer: Not currently — the swimming and beach area remains closed due to a lifeguard shortage. Boating (10 mph limit) and fishing are open, with day and season passes sold on-site.

faq.question: Is the Peoples State Forest Nature Museum open?
faq.answer: Yes, seasonally and free of charge: Memorial Day through mid-June, Saturday and Sunday 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; mid-June through Labor Day, Friday-Monday 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; Labor Day through mid-October, Saturday and Sunday 10 a.m.-4 p.m. It's closed roughly mid-October through Memorial Day.

faq.question: Where can I eat and stay in Barkhamsted?
faq.answer: The Log House Restaurant has served Route 44 since 1973, and Brass Horse Cafe pairs a full kitchen with Sunday-afternoon live music. In Riverton, the Royal Coachman Tavern serves the Old Riverton Inn's restaurant, and the inn itself — ten rooms in a building dating from 1796 — is the town's only lodging.

places.name: Peoples State Forest
places.address: Off Route 20 or Route 318, Barkhamsted, CT 06063
places.summary: Roughly 3,000 acres along the West Branch Farmington River with hiking, fishing, canoeing, picnicking, cross-country skiing and snowmobiling. Home to the Lighthouse Archaeological Site and a stone Nature Museum built by the CCC in 1935, open free Memorial Day through mid-October with seasonal hours. Phone (860) 379-2469.

places.name: American Legion State Forest
places.address: Off Route 20 or Route 318, Barkhamsted, CT 06063
places.summary: Sits across the Farmington River from Peoples State Forest, with hiking, fishing, canoeing and kayaking, picnicking, cross-country skiing and snowmobiling. The Austin F. Hawes Memorial Campground sits by the riverbank; reservations through Reserve America. Phone (860) 379-0922.

places.name: Lake McDonough Recreation Area
places.summary: Run by the Metropolitan District Commission below Saville Dam, with boating (10 mph limit) and shore or boat fishing; the swimming beach remains closed for a lifeguard shortage. 2026 season runs weekends from April 11, then daily 10 a.m.-8 p.m. from May 1 through September 7. Day passes $10 residents / $20 non-residents, credit or debit only.

places.name: Squire's Tavern (Barkhamsted Historical Society)
places.summary: The restored tavern headquarters the Barkhamsted Historical Society, which also stewards Merrill Tavern and the seasonal Center Schoolhouse. Open Wednesdays 9 a.m.-noon and Sundays 1-4 p.m. Phone (860) 738-2456.

places.name: Lighthouse Archaeological Site
places.address: Within Peoples State Forest, off East River Road, Barkhamsted, CT 06063
places.summary: Remains of the mixed-race community founded around 1740 by Mary "Molly" Barber and James Chaugham, a Narragansett man — cellar holes and a graveyard survive along the Jessie Gerard Trail. Designated a State Archaeological Preserve in 2008 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places since April 1991.

places.name: Saville Dam and Barkhamsted Reservoir
places.summary: A stone-and-earth dam named for MDC chief engineer Caleb Mills Saville, completed in 1940 to impound a 30-billion-gallon reservoir; water first flowed to Hartford on December 21, 1944. Flooding Barkhamsted Hollow displaced roughly 1,000 residents. Watershed land — a scenic drive-by and walking stop, not for swimming or boating.

places.name: Log House Restaurant
places.summary: A family-owned roadside institution on Route 44 in continuous operation since 1973, from steaks and seafood to homestyle soups at family-style prices. Open daily 7:30 a.m.-3 p.m. Phone (860) 379-8937.

places.name: Brass Horse Cafe
places.summary: A casual American cafe and bar on Route 44 with bands every Sunday afternoon. Kitchen hours Tuesday-Saturday 11:30 a.m.-8 p.m., Sunday to 8:30 p.m., closed Monday; cafe stays open later. Phone (860) 738-2017.

places.name: The Royal Coachman Tavern at The Old Riverton Inn
places.summary: The dining room and tavern inside the Old Riverton Inn, in a building the inn dates to 1796. Dine-in and takeout Wednesday-Thursday 4-8 p.m., Friday-Saturday noon-9 p.m., Sunday noon-7 p.m., closed Monday-Tuesday. Phone (860) 379-8678.

places.name: The Riverton General Store
places.summary: A village deli in the heart of Riverton, a few steps from the Old Riverton Inn and the Farmington River, known locally for sandwiches. No published hours — call ahead. Phone (860) 379-0811.

places.name: The Old Riverton Inn
places.summary: Ten non-smoking guest rooms in a building the inn dates to 1796, most with views of Riverton village and the Farmington River. The Village Hall function room seats up to 100 for weddings and events. No elevator. Phone (860) 379-8678.

links.note: Barkhamsted borders New Hartford, three miles southwest of Lake McDonough along Route 219.
US Route 44 links Barkhamsted west through Winsted and Norfolk toward North Canaan.
